what_happened: On a straight multi-lane highway, after handoff the policy braked for no clear reason (16.8 to 11.4 m/s with no lead close ahead) and drifted left out of its lane centre. Its front-left clipped actor 1, which was travelling alongside in the left lane. The rear contact came later, most likely from traffic behind reacting to the unneeded braking.

In slow, dense highway traffic the ego followed actor 12 closely (about 4–5 m) as 12 sat between lanes just ahead and to the right. On a RIGHT command, the ego sped up from 3.1 to 3.8 m/s and steered right toward 12's lane, and its front-right corner hit 12's rear-left corner.

On a multi-lane highway, the policy's planned path bent left toward the next lane over, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and later RIGHT. The ego drifted into that lane at about 4.6 m/s and its front hit actor 41, which was alongside and slightly ahead in that lane, at 7.4 s.

On a straight multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT, the policy took over at 4.6 s, braked from 16.8 to 11.5 m/s for no visible reason, and steered left out of its lane. It hit actor 1, which was beside it in the left lane, with its front. The car that later hit the ego's rear was probably following it and caught out by the unneeded braking.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the ego braked from about 17 to 11 m/s and drifted left out of its lane, even though the command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Its front-left corner hit actor 1, which was in the adjacent left lane. The rear contact flagged in the data came after this front collision.

On a wet multi-lane highway at about 5 m/s, the policy's planned path (orange) bent left, away from the recorded path that stayed in its lane and drifted slightly right. The ego moved into the adjacent left lane and its front hit vehicle 41, which was travelling beside it in that lane, at 7.4 s.

On a straight multi-lane highway in the rain, the policy's planned path bent left and the ego drifted out of its lane, toward the recorded path's left, into the next lane. At about 4.9 m/s it ran its front into pickup 41, which was in that lane just ahead and to the left. The camera view was clean before contact, so the policy is at fault for an unforced merge into an occupied lane.

In slow freeway traffic, the ego was following vehicle 12 at about 4 m. Instead of staying in lane like the human, it steered right toward 12's lane and sped up, and its front hit 12's left rear quarter. Separately, a vehicle behind hit the ego's rear at some point.

In slow freeway traffic, the ego followed lead vehicle 12 in its own lane at about 3–3.8 m/s and never braked. The 3.7–4.9 m gap shown is too short for two car lengths, so the ego's front was already touching 12's rear by 6.5 s (front collision flagged) and it was still pushing into 12 at 8.5 s while its plan bent right, toward 12, on a RIGHT command.

In slow freeway traffic (about 3–4 m/s), the ego followed actor 12 only about 4 m behind and touched its rear at about 6.4 s. It then sped up from 3.0 to 4.0 m/s while 12 was still just ahead and slightly to the right. At 8.4 s its front corner hit 12 again while it drifted left of the route toward actor 56.

The ego was replaying the recorded drive at about 8 m/s, closing on slower lead vehicle 1 in the same lane (the gap fell from 17 m to about 5 m). The policy took over at 4.6 s, and the front collision with vehicle 1 was flagged at 4.8 s. The ego was still exactly on the human trajectory (0.0 m off), so this collision was set up before handoff, likely because the log and the reconstructed actor's box overlap, and the policy had no real chance to avoid it.

From 1.8 s to 4.6 s the ego was replaying the human log at about 8 m/s, and in that time the gap to lead vehicle 1 in its lane shrank steadily from 17.4 m to about 5 m. The policy took over at 4.6 s and the front collision with vehicle 1 was recorded at 4.8 s, so the crash was already unavoidable at handoff, most likely because the replayed lead actor doesn't match the recorded drive.

Before handoff, the ego replayed the recorded trajectory at about 7.9 m/s and closed steadily on slower lead vehicle 1 in its lane, from a 17 m gap down to about 5 m. The policy took over at 4.6 s, only 0.2 s before the front collision at 4.8 s, which was not enough time to stop. The collision was set up by the replay before handoff, not caused by the policy.

Before handoff the ego replayed the recorded human drive at a steady ~8 m/s, while the gap to lead vehicle 1 in its lane shrank from 17 m to about 5 m. The policy took over at 4.6 s and the front collision with vehicle 1 came just 0.2 s later, still exactly on the recorded path. The crash was effectively locked in before handoff, most likely because the lead actor's simulated motion did not match the real drive.
